lead: Seasonal names and learning books offer different ways to understand Koya, from shared food to the work of reading.

proposed_sections.title: Begin with a language and a place

paragraphs.text: Koya belongs to the Dravidian language family. In Odisha, SCSTRTI’s community profile places it in Malkangiri. That geographical starting point leads into a wider written world: the learning books below use different scripts and draw on contributors from different states.

proposed_sections.title: A season marked by what is eaten

paragraphs.text: Two entries in the profile’s festival table make the agricultural connection concrete. Kurumpandu marks the first eating of small millets; Sikudpandu concerns new beans. These names connect an occasion with a particular food becoming available. They offer more to ask about than a general label such as harvest festival, without supplying a calendar for a visit.

Music also has a place of practice in the account. It describes singing associated with the girls’ dormitory, Pikin-Kudma, and an open space opposite the dormitory used for dance. The same profile says this institution has declined. Its description preserves a connection between learning together and performance, rather than proving that every village maintains it today.

proposed_sections.title: A forest, a mirror and a letter

paragraphs.text: The CIIL–NCERT Koya Primer of 9 March 2024 uses Telugu script. It credits Peesodi Kannaiah and Payam Venkataratnam, whose listed roles are in Telangana, and Karam Narayanarao Dora and Komaram Sitaramaraju, whose roles are in Andhra Pradesh. The contributor page locates this particular resource within a teaching network that extends beyond Odisha.

Open it to printed page 3. A forest picture sits beside a short passage and word labels; below are a mirror, a group dancing and a road. Along the bottom, a repeated letter grows progressively fainter for writing practice. A learner moves from recognising a picture to finding its written label and trying the letter. The dance image is a learning example; its location and occasion are not established here.

For an Odia-linked resource, CIIL’s catalogue lists a separate Koya–Odia Primer from 2025, edited by Narayan Choudhary and colleagues. Its ISBN is 978-81-977442-8-0. The listing identifies another edition; its lessons have not been inspected for this article.

proposed_sections.title: Three columns, more than one kind of question

paragraphs.text: The 2018 Malkangiri booklet sets English, Odia and Koya alongside one another. Beyond its opening pronouns, it includes questions and everyday sentences. Follow an example across the columns with a willing reader, then ask how they would use it. The original compilers remain credited below.
